title: Mean change under a sign restriction
statement: Let $f$ be a real-valued function on the $n$-dimensional sign cube, and suppose it is not Fourier-regular at degree at most $k$ with tolerance $\varepsilon$; that is, some nonempty set of coordinates of size at most $k$ has a Fourier coefficient of absolute value greater than $\varepsilon$. Then there is a set $J$ of coordinates whose complement has size at most $k$, and an assignment of signs to the coordinates outside $J$, such that restricting $f$ to that assignment changes its mean by more than $\varepsilon$ in absolute value.
hypotheses_covered: $f$ is real-valued on the $n$-dimensional sign cube
Failure of Fourier regularity with parameters $\varepsilon$ and $k$
